chain: T1 (rule): daily schedules with weekend handling skip weekend occurrences instead of moving them (fixes duplicate Fridays/Mondays and next dates before the start).
T2 (consumer): new handler schedule/get-dates-in-range { config, start, end } -> days, following the schedule date rules (weekend moves, T1 skips), judged by the final day.

T3 (rule): optional holidays: YYYY-MM-DD[] in the recurring configuration, treated like weekend days when weekend handling is on (moved to the nearest free day in the configured direction, skipped for daily).
T4 (build): holidays entries may be MM-DD, meaning that day every year; full dates still work, mixed lists allowed.
design.why_decision_level: In R the weekend arithmetic (date + mode) is already shared by every copy (study2-variants.md honesty item 2), so a change to the arithmetic alone would reach every copy in both conditions and could not show a missed copy. T1 and T3 need information the arithmetic does not receive (the frequency; the holiday list), so each site that decides whether and how the rule applies has to change. This holds in F as well: F's callers map their own fields onto the helper's rule object, so a new input has to be mapped at each caller there too. This is a property of the frozen variants, recorded here, not tuned for either condition.
design.statements: Behaviour only, written as a maintainer would phrase the request. They name the new handler and the new configuration field (public interface the tests need) but no file, function, location or number of places; rule steps say only that the rule must hold wherever the app works out a schedule's dates.
design.consumers: next-date (schedule/create, then the stored next date), upcoming-dates (schedule/get-upcoming-dates), budget-template (budget/dry-run-category-template on a schedule template), dates-in-range (the T2 handler, from T2 on). The template's two copies are one consumer; its T1/T3 tests use months that make a tree with only one of the two copies updated fail, and avoid months where the next-date site would change the template's count.
design.tests: Through public handlers on a real (test) database; nothing mocked (no network boundary in this zone). Dates are fixed; 'today' is set with MockDate where a handler reads it. Imports exist in both R and F; no test names a helper of F or a copy of R. Upcoming-date assertions on daily schedules check a prefix plus no weekend/holiday day and no repeated day, so both readings of 'next N dates' (N after skipping, or skipping within the first N) pass.

implementation.R_shape: Kept R's per-site style: each site (next date, upcoming dates, both template copies, and the T2 handler) decides inline whether the daily skip applies; the shared weekend arithmetic getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays argument (T3) and a shared isWeekendOrHoliday predicate backs the skip checks, so T4 (MM-DD) changes only that predicate.
implementation.F_shape: WeekendRule gains frequency (T1) and holidays (T3); applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay return null for an occurrence the rule drops (daily schedules); each caller maps its own fields onto the rule, the T2 handler calls applyWeekendRule.
implementation.shared_by_both: The parsed schedule data (rule-utils parseRecurDate) carries frequency (T1) and holidays (T3); RecurConfig gains holidays?: string[] (T3). Existing weekend moves are reproduced exactly by stepping day by day (Sat/Sun after -> Monday, before -> Friday).
interpretations: upcoming dates on a daily schedule return `count` dates after skipping (reads up to count*7 occurrences).

getNextDate on a daily schedule with weekend handling looks up to 7 occurrences ahead for a kept one; for a finished schedule it falls back to the last kept occurrence (as before for the last occurrence); null if none.
schedule/get-dates-in-range reads occurrences from start-(7+holidays) to end+(7+holidays) days, applies the rule, keeps final days within [start, end], dedupes and sorts; start > end returns [].
Budget template: dropped occurrences are not counted; the loop stops on the base date when the occurrence is dropped.
